answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to hold a costly, non-transferable work history — a relic of past verified tasks — before it earns voting weight. Newcomers start on a small island of low-stakes jobs where mistakes are cheap and reputation accrues slowly; only after a long, checkable record do they graduate to high-value work. Attackers who spin up a thousand fresh identities face the same slow climb each time, so the fable of effortless duplication collapses: cloning accounts multiplies the cost, not the reward.
